facts: The appropriate Government may at any time refer an industrial dispute to a Board for promoting a settlement thereof or to a court for inquiry.

If the dispute relates to any matter specified in the Second Schedule and is not likely to affect more than one hundred workmen, the appropriate Government may make the reference to a Labour Court under clause (c).

The Central Government may refer an industrial dispute to a National Tribunal if it involves any question of national importance or is of such a nature that industrial establishments situated in more than one State are likely to be interested in, or affected by, such dispute.

Where the parties to an industrial dispute apply for a reference of the dispute to a Board, Court, Labour Court, Tribunal or National Tribunal, the appropriate Government shall make the reference accordingly.
issues: What is the scope of the Central Government's power to refer an industrial dispute to a National Tribunal?

Can the appropriate Government refer an industrial dispute to a Labour Court or Tribunal if it relates to any matter specified in the Second Schedule and is not likely to affect more than one hundred workmen?

Is the Central Government required to refer an industrial dispute to a National Tribunal if it involves any question of national importance or is of such a nature that industrial establishments situated in more than one State are likely to be interested in, or affected by, such dispute?
court_reasoning: The court held that the Central Government has the power to refer an industrial dispute to a National Tribunal if it involves any question of national importance or is of such a nature that industrial establishments situated in more than one State are likely to be interested in, or affected by, such dispute.

The court also held that the appropriate Government may refer an industrial dispute to a Labour Court or Tribunal if it relates to any matter specified in the Second Schedule and is not likely to affect more than one hundred workmen.
holding: The Central Government has the power to refer an industrial dispute to a National Tribunal if it involves any question of national importance or is of such a nature that industrial establishments situated in more than one State are likely to be interested in, or affected by, such dispute.

The appropriate Government may refer an industrial dispute to a Labour Court or Tribunal if it relates to any matter specified in the Second Schedule and is not likely to affect more than one hundred workmen.
